description.summary: Bohemian Grove is a 2,700-acre (1,100 ha) campground near Monte Rio, California, owned by the private Bohemian Club, which hosts an annual two-week summer encampment attended by political, business, and cultural elites and is the focus of long-running conspiracy theories.
description.full: Bohemian Grove is a 2,700-acre (1,100 ha) redwood retreat owned by the San Francisco-based Bohemian Club at 20601 Bohemian Avenue, Monte Rio, Sonoma County, California. The Bohemian Club was founded in 1872; the summer encampment tradition dates to 1878, when fewer than 100 members gathered at a redwood site to honor departing actor Henry Edwards. The club has rented the current site since 1893 and purchased it in 1899 from Melvin Cyrus Meeker. Each July, members and guests — restricted to men — convene for two weeks of theatrical productions ('Grove Plays'), 'Lakeside Talks' lectures, fireside camps, and informal networking. The encampment opens with the 'Cremation of Care', a torchlit allegorical performance staged before a 30-foot concrete owl shrine designed by sculptor Haig Patigian (constructed in the late 1920s) in which a humanoid effigy representing 'Dull Care' is symbolically burned. Bohemian Grove has been documented as a venue for genuinely consequential meetings — most notably a September 1942 Manhattan Project planning session attended by Ernest Lawrence and J. Robert Oppenheimer, and a July 1950 introduction between Dwight Eisenhower and Richard Nixon — but conspiracy theorists, most prominently Alex Jones in his 2000 hidden-camera infiltration, have characterized the Cremation of Care as occult or sacrificial. Mainstream journalists, sociologists, and infiltrating reporters such as Philip Weiss (1989, Spy magazine) have generally described the rituals as theatrical and the Grove as a study in elite male sociology rather than a site of literal occult practice.

etymology.origin: Named after the Bohemian Club of San Francisco, founded in 1872 by journalists, artists, and musicians who styled themselves 'Bohemians'. The encampment grounds are sited in a coastal redwood grove, hence 'Bohemian Grove'.
etymology.meaning: 'Bohemian' here refers to the 19th-century artistic/literary self-identification, not to Bohemia in central Europe.
etymology.first_use: 1878 (first encampment); the term 'Bohemian Grove' for the current site dates from the club's lease beginning in 1893.

features.description: The property contains roughly 160 acres of old-growth coast redwoods, some over 1,000 years old
30-foot reinforced-concrete statue of an owl, designed by Haig Patigian, used as the focal piece of the Cremation of Care ceremony
Approximately 118 named camps (as of 2007), each with cabins, dining lodges, and themed identities

physical.morphology: A wooded retreat property in the Russian River watershed, Sonoma County, with rustic permanent infrastructure (lodges, theatrical stages, an outdoor amphitheater, and the Owl Shrine) maintained year-round.

patterns: Two-week summer encampment in mid-to-late July, with shorter spring and fall events
Members-and-guests-only access; women historically excluded as members
Opens with the 'Cremation of Care' ceremony at the Owl Shrine
Programming combines lectures ('Lakeside Talks'), Grove Plays, and informal camp life

range.description: A single fixed property near Monte Rio, Sonoma County, California, in the redwood country of the Russian River.

hotspots.name: Bohemian Grove
hotspots.notes: The 2,700-acre Bohemian Club property and site of the annual encampment.

first_recorded.source: Bohemian Club records of the first 'High Jinks' encampment honoring Henry Edwards

peak_activity_periods.description: Heightened public attention following Alex Jones's 2000 infiltration video

temporal.seasonal_patterns: Main encampment falls in mid-to-late July; smaller spring 'Jinks' and other events occur throughout the year.

origins.cultural_roots: Founded as a social club for journalists, artists, writers, and musicians in 1870s San Francisco; rapidly broadened to include patrons from finance, industry, and government.
origins.earliest_accounts: The Bohemian Club was founded in 1872; the first encampment in the redwoods dates to 1878.
origins.folklore_connections: The 'Cremation of Care' draws on Greco-Roman theatrical motifs and 19th-century pageant traditions; conspiracy framings retroactively read it as occult.

First summer encampment, fewer than 100 members, honoring departing actor Henry Edwards
timeline.significance: Beginning of the Bohemian Grove tradition
Founding of the Grove's signature opening ritual

timeline.event: Club begins renting the current Monte Rio site
timeline.significance: The Grove acquires its present geographic identity

timeline.event: Club purchases the property from Melvin Cyrus Meeker
timeline.significance: Permanent ownership of the redwood grove

timeline.event: 'Cremation of Care' separated from other Grove Plays as its own opening ritual
Manhattan Project planning meeting at the Grove involving Ernest Lawrence and J. Robert Oppenheimer

timeline.significance: Frequently cited example of political networking at the Grove

Alex Jones and Mike Hanson covertly film the Cremation of Care ceremony

timeline.source: Infowars/Alex Jones, 'Dark Secrets: Inside Bohemian Grove' (2000)

history.modern_era: The Grove has continued to host its annual encampment uninterrupted in the 21st century, drawing intermittent protests, discrimination lawsuits over its men-only membership, and a steady stream of conspiracy media. Mainstream coverage (e.g., the Washington Post, The New York Times, and academic sociology by G. William Domhoff) treats it as an empirically real elite-networking institution, while conspiracy-theory media continues to frame it as a site of occult ritual.

physical.name: Owl Shrine
physical.description: 30-foot reinforced-concrete owl statue designed by Bohemian Club member and sculptor Haig Patigian; serves as the backdrop for the Cremation of Care ceremony.
physical.analysis: Photographed in the 1989 Weiss reporting and 2000 Jones video; existence and design are not in dispute.

video.name: 'Dark Secrets: Inside Bohemian Grove'
video.description: Hidden-camera footage of the Cremation of Care ceremony filmed covertly by Alex Jones and Mike Hanson.
video.analysis: Authenticity of the footage is generally accepted; Jones's interpretation of the ritual as 'mock human sacrifice' is widely rejected by mainstream commentators and former attendees.

documentary.name: 'Inside Bohemian Grove' (Spy magazine)
documentary.description: First-person infiltration account by reporter Philip Weiss describing the camps, talks, and Cremation of Care.
documentary.analysis: Considered the most detailed contemporaneous mainstream-press account of the encampment.

paranormal.name: Occult ritual / mock human sacrifice
paranormal.description: Asserts that the Cremation of Care is a literal occult ceremony invoking Moloch via the giant owl shrine, used to bond elites in collective transgression.
evidence_cited: Hidden-camera footage of the 2000 Cremation of Care

scientific.name: Elite networking institution
scientific.description: Sociologists frame the Grove as a documented mechanism of elite cohesion, where political, corporate, and military leaders form personal ties that influence policy outcomes.
evidence_cited: Domhoff, The Bohemian Grove and Other Retreats (1974)
Cross-membership data with corporate boards and federal advisory committees
Documented meetings (e.g., 1942 Manhattan Project planning, 1950 Eisenhower–Nixon introduction)

skeptical.name: Theatrical pageant, not ritual
skeptical.description: The Cremation of Care is a 19th-century-style allegorical pageant in the tradition of Grove Plays — performative theater rather than literal religious ceremony.
evidence_cited: Documented Grove Play scripts and program books

traditions: Cremation of Care ceremony at the Owl Shrine
folklore.beliefs: Conspiracy traditions hold that policy is decided in informal Grove conversations and ratified through occult ceremony; mainstream observers hold that the Grove functions as elite social infrastructure rather than as a decision-making body.
